description:
`SegmentedControl` is a horizontal bar of mutually exclusive options. Use it to switch between two to five related views or filters in the same context. Only one option is selected at a time. Every option needs a `value`, the string that identifies it in `value`, `defaultValue` and `onChange`. ### Accessibility `SegmentedControl` renders a `radiogroup` and each option is a `radio`. Give the group a name with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and give every icon-only option a `screenReaderLabel`. Only the selected option (or the first one, when nothing is selected) is in the tab order. The arrow keys move focus to the next or previous option without selecting it, so users can browse before they choose. Space and Enter select the focused option. The arrow keys stop at the first and last option instead of wrapping, and Tab leaves the control. In right-to-left layouts, Arrow Left and Arrow Right swap. Home and End jump to the first and last option. Options must be direct children of `SegmentedControl`. ```js --- type: example --- ``` ### Controlled and uncontrolled Pass `defaultValue` and let `SegmentedControl` track the selection. Or pass `value` together with `onChange` to control it yourself. `onChange` receives the event and the `value` of the option the user selected. ```js --- type: example --- const Example = () => { const [view, setView] = useState('grid') return ( setView(value)} > Selected: {view} ) } render() ``` ### Sizes The `size` prop accepts `medium` (the default), `large`, and `small`. Use `medium` in most places, `large` where the control needs more prominence, and `small` in compact toolbars or inline controls. ```js --- type: example ---
``` ### Text, icons, and both An option shows text with `renderLabel`, an icon with `renderIcon`, or both. Don't mix icon-only and text-only options in one control. An option with no `renderLabel` needs a `screenReaderLabel`. Without it, screen readers can't name the option. ```js --- type: example ---
} renderLabel="Grid" /> } renderLabel="List" /> } screenReaderLabel="Grid view" /> } screenReaderLabel="List view" />
``` ### Overflow When the options don't fit the available width, they stay on one row and scroll. Set `renderPreviousLabel` and `renderNextLabel` to also show arrow buttons over the edges of the control, each only while there are options to scroll to in that direction. Both labels are needed so screen readers can name the arrows. The control fills at most the width of its container, so put it in a container of the width you want to limit it to. ```js --- type: example ---
{['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep'].map((month) => ( ))}
``` ### Guidelines ```js --- type: embed --- ```

children.description: The `SegmentedControl.Option` elements to render, as direct children.

value.description: The value of the selected option, which makes the component controlled.

defaultValue.description: The value of the option selected on first render when uncontrolled.

onChange.description: Called with the event and the value of the option the user selected.

size.description: The size of the control and its options.

renderPreviousLabel.description: The accessible name of the arrow that scrolls back to the earlier options. The arrows only appear when both labels are set and the options don't fit the available width.

renderNextLabel.description: The accessible name of the arrow that scrolls on to the later options.
